title: Usage-pattern-driven resize recommender for Dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, explainable recommender that suggests per-pool resizing actions (scale up/down, change commit size, or change autoscale policy) based on observed throughput and latency patterns. The recommender should target cost-per-concurrent-request reduction while preserving throughput guarantees and SLOs for Dedicated customers.

Scope: ingest historical metrics (token throughput, request rate, percentiles of p99 latency, GPU utilization, queued requests), run heuristics + ML signal to produce ranked suggestions, present recommendations via Console and API, and provide an audit trail with expected cost delta and risk.

Out of scope for MVP: automatic enforcement (recommendations are surfaced as proposals for operator approval), cross-customer multi-tenant optimization, and model-level kernel reconfiguration.

Why now: multiple enterprise customers reported periodic overprovisioning for steady low-traffic windows and missed opportunities to reduce commit sizes during stable workloads. Existing fleet advisors are batch-oriented and not surfaced in Console with clear cost impact modeling. This ticket delivers product-visible, action-focused guidance tied to Dedicated controls and autoscaling policies.
tasks: Design metrics schema and storage (timeseries + aggregated windows)
Implement data pipeline to compute 1h/6h/24h profiles per pool
Prototype heuristic rules (min headroom, safe downscale cadence, penalty for SLO breach)
Integrate recommender API endpoint and pagination
Add Console panel showing suggested actions, expected monthly savings, and risk score
Create telemetry event for accepted/ignored suggestions
Write integration tests and load test the recommender compute job
Prepare rollout plan and canary to 3 beta customers
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces suggestions for >=90% of active Dedicated pools in test org
Console shows expected monthly cost delta and 95% confidence interval
No increase in SLO breaches in canary orgs for 14 days after applying recommended conservative resizes
APIs and UI have audit entries for all suggestions and customer actions
Documentation (Confluence + Console help) published before beta rollout

decision_log: Prefer explainable heuristic-first approach instead of opaque ML model for MVP to facilitate trust and debugging.
Recommendations are proposals only; no automatic enforcement for GA to preserve customer control and legal constraints.
Include an explicit 'risk score' and 'confidence band' in every suggestion to communicate uncertainty.
Cooldown policy: minimum 48 hours between automated recommended resizes unless customer explicitly approves immediate action.
tradeoffs: Heuristic-first reduces potential accuracy compared to an ML-driven recommender but shortens time-to-alpha and eases regulatory review.
Conservative defaults may under-capture savings initially; we accept slower savings realization to avoid SLO regressions.
Maintaining per-pool state increases metadata overhead in storage; tradeoff versus recomputing from raw timeseries on demand.
